title: Lab 10 — Quiz 2
subtitle: Unknown ID Part 1 — dichotomous key and skills

questions.prompt: Using this dichotomous key: a Gram-negative bacillus is lactose positive and citrate negative. What is it?
questions.explanation: Gram − → bacillus → lactose + → citrate − = E. coli.

why.C: Proteus vulgaris is lactose − and citrate −.

questions.prompt: Using this key: a Gram-negative bacillus is lactose negative and citrate positive. What is it?
questions.explanation: Gram − → bacillus → lactose − → citrate + = Serratia marcescens.

why.D: E. coli is lactose + and citrate −.

questions.prompt: Using this key: a Gram-negative bacillus is lactose positive and citrate positive. What is it?
questions.explanation: Gram − → bacillus → lactose + → citrate + = Klebsiella pneumoniae.

questions.prompt: Using this key: a Gram-negative bacillus is lactose negative and citrate negative. What is it?
questions.explanation: Gram − → bacillus → lactose − → citrate − = Proteus vulgaris.

questions.prompt: Using this key: which organism is a Gram-negative coccus?
Using this key: a Gram-positive organism is salt tolerant and ferments mannitol. What is it?
questions.explanation: Gram + → salt tolerant (yes) → mannitol + = S. aureus.

why.A: S. epidermidis is salt tolerant but mannitol negative.

questions.prompt: Using this key: a Gram-positive organism is NOT salt tolerant and is beta-hemolytic. What is it?
questions.explanation: Gram + → not salt tolerant → hemolysis: beta = S. pyogenes; alpha = S. pneumoniae.

questions.prompt: Using this key: a Gram-positive organism is NOT salt tolerant and is alpha-hemolytic. What is it?
questions.explanation: Gram + → not salt tolerant → alpha = S. pneumoniae.

questions.prompt: Your unknown grows pink on MacConkey and stays green/no growth on citrate. Its Gram stain shows pink rods. Using the unknowns key, identify it.
questions.explanation: Pink rods = Gram − bacillus; pink on MacConkey = lactose +; no citrate growth = citrate − → E. coli.

why.B: Klebsiella would grow and turn citrate blue.
why.C: Proteus would be yellow-orange (lactose −) on MacConkey.

questions.prompt: Your unknown is a Gram-negative rod that is yellow-orange on MacConkey and turns citrate agar blue. Identify it.
questions.explanation: Yellow-orange = lactose −; blue citrate = citrate + → Serratia marcescens.

why.A: E. coli is pink on MacConkey and citrate −.

questions.prompt: For the Gram stain skills assessment, what goes on the slide along with your unknown?

options.text: Control smears of a known Gram-positive and a known Gram-negative
A negative wet mount of the same unknown culture
An endospore-stained smear of the unknown culture
Only the unknown smear, with no control smears

questions.explanation: Slide G: control smears (known G+ and known G−) plus a smear of the unknown. Flag the instructor after focusing to oil immersion on the control smear.

why.B: The assessment uses a Gram stain with controls.
why.C: The slide has controls plus the unknown.
why.D: Known G+ and G− control smears are included.

questions.prompt: For the streak plating skills assessment in Lab 10, which medium is streaked?
questions.explanation: Obtain a sterile MacConkey plate, label it (initials, table #, Client ID) and perform the quadrant streak method.

why.A: The Lab 10 assessment uses a sterile MacConkey plate.
why.B: Blood agar is used for hemolysis in Lab 11.
why.D: Citrate is inoculated as a slant, not streaked for the assessment.

questions.prompt: What are the two goals of laboratory testing in the unknown labs?

options.text: Count the cells and measure turbidity
Stain the cells and sterilize the media
Identify the pathogen and identify effective treatment(s)
Collect the specimen and label it

questions.explanation: Goal 1: identify the pathogen (phenotype and biochemistry). Goal 2: identify effective treatments (antimicrobial sensitivity testing).

why.B: Those are lab techniques, not the goals.

questions.prompt: In a dichotomous key, identifying a microbe 'by behavior' means using:
questions.explanation: Identification by appearance = phenotype; by behavior = biochemistry.

why.B: Symptoms guide specimen choice; behavior = biochemistry.
why.D: The microscope is a tool for appearance.

questions.prompt: Which statement about specimen handling is FALSE?

options.text: The pathogen may die before it can be cultured
Resident microbiota in a specimen can never cause a false positive
Resident microbiota may overgrow the pathogen
Contamination may interfere with lab findings
Positive and negative controls are run regularly

questions.explanation: False positive = a resident microbe is mistakenly identified as the cause. False negative = the pathogen is missed.
